title: Maple pecan cookies
subtitle: soft, chewy cookies with maple syrup and toasted pecans
excerpt: Maple pecan cookies are soft, chewy cookies with maple syrup stirred through the dough and toasted pecans folded in. The maple syrup adds a gentle caramel sweetness and helps the cookies stay soft and chewy after baking. The pecans add a buttery, slightly bitter crunch. The cookies spread as they bake and come out with a crinkled top and a slightly tacky centre.
sourceNotes: Maple and pecan as a baking combination documented in North American cookbooks from the nineteenth century onward. The drop-cookie method for soft, chewy cookies is standard American home baking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked cookies in an airtight container for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 5 days. Best the day of baking.

content.text: Maple pecan cookies are soft drop cookies where maple syrup replaces some of the sugar in the dough. The syrup keeps the cookies chewy and slightly tacky at the centre after baking. Chilling the dough before baking stops the cookies from spreading too thin and gives a thicker, chewier result.
Beat the softened butter, brown sugar, and maple syrup together until well combined, about 2 minutes. Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Fold in the flour and bicarbonate of soda until just combined. Fold in the toasted pecans.
Chill the dough in the fridge for 30 minutes. This stops the cookies spreading too much.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Scoop rounded tablespoons of dough onto the prepared trays, spacing them about 5 cm apart. Flatten each slightly with your palm.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until the edges are set and golden but the centres still look slightly underdone. They firm up as they cool. Leave on the tray for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack.

attrs.problem: Cookies spreading into thin, flat discs
attrs.avoid: Avoid skipping the chill time; warm dough with butter and syrup spreads very quickly in the oven.
attrs.fix: Chill the dough for a full 30 minutes. If your kitchen is very warm, chill for 45 minutes.

attrs.problem: Cookies hard and dry rather than chewy
attrs.avoid: Avoid baking until the centres look set; by then the centres will be hard once cooled.
attrs.fix: Remove from the oven when the centres still look very slightly underdone. The residual heat of the tray sets them to a chewy result over the next 5 minutes.
